jobs.description:
Brief Description

PRIMARY FUNCTION

The Lead Community Health Worker (Lead CHW) contributes to meeting patients’ comprehensive needs, including social determinants of health (SDOH) and direct medical services. Under the Primary Care Medical Home (PCMH) model, the Lead CHW contributes to patient recruitment, education, navigation, social support, medical follow-up, care coordination, and integration. Chronic disease management and risk factor reduction are often the focus of these efforts, with emphasis on proven chronic disease prevention and control interventions.

In addition to direct community health work responsibilities, this position serves as the central point of accountability for patient flow across clinical care and community-based services. The Lead CHW translates provider care plans into actionable next steps, oversees daily CHW activities, and resolves breakdowns in referrals, care coordination, and system workflows. This role works across clinical teams, CHWs, and health information systems to close care gaps, prioritize work in real time, and ensure follow-through on care plans.

Join the Malama I Ke Ola Health Center Team!

Team-Based Work Environment
90 Day Introductory Period
Awesome benefits

Medical, Dental, Vision, life insurance, short & long-term disability, and 403(b) Retirement Plan, FSA, and other voluntary benefits

Vacation, Holiday and Sick Benefits

LEAD COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER

with Clinical Navigation Liaison Responsibilities

Essential Duties And Functions

Patient Flow & Care Navigation

The Lead CHW serves as the primary driver of patient movement across clinical and community-based care pathways:

Ensure patients move efficiently from identification of need to completed services across clinical and community-based systems.
Translate provider care plans into clear, actionable tasks for CHWs and care teams.
Monitor and address breakdowns in care pathways, including delays, missed follow-ups, and incomplete referrals.
Prioritize patient needs and direct CHW activities in real time to address urgent or high-risk situations.
Identify High-Needs Patients in collaboration with the Medical Provider; contact all identified High-Needs Patients prior to their next visit to assess whether previous care plan objectives have been completed.
Coordinate pre-visit planning with RN and Medical Provider; review protocols due for the patient.
Support navigation of SDOH needs, ensuring patients are connected to appropriate internal and external resources.
Care Coordination & Community Health Services

The Lead CHW provides direct patient services at the health center and in the community such as:

Care coordination to implement and monitor care management plans
Working with patients, families, caregivers, and community partners
Resource identification, goal setting, and assistance with self-monitoring
Culturally and age-appropriate education in multiple languages, including instructional materials, health screens, and clarification of care plans in compliance with clinical protocols
Patient recruitment: contacting individuals who have not yet established care and informing them about available services
Assistance with appointment scheduling, including contacting patients with no-show or canceled appointment status and rescheduling.
Psychosocial support
Translation and/or interpretation services as qualified
Transportation coordination
Financial assistance to access complementary and alternative care options
Taking vital signs
Assisting with patient-related paperwork
Check, maintain, and report inventory supplies to the Program Manager
Referral Management & Closed-Loop Coordination
Ensure referrals (internal and external) are completed, tracked, and followed through to resolution.
Define and maintain standards for closed-loop referrals and care coordination.
Work with clinical teams to clarify unclear or incomplete referrals and care plans.
Identify and resolve barriers to patient access.
CHW Supervision & Team Leadership

The Lead CHW directly supervises Community Health Workers.

Oversee daily workflow and task prioritization for CHWs; provide real-time direction on patient engagement strategies and care plan execution.
Prepare and publish work schedules; approve timecards and time-off requests in compliance with pay policies.
Recruit, select, train, manage, and motivate CHWs; provide performance feedback during 1:1 sessions and at fiscal year-end.
Ensure CHW activities align with active clinical care plans and organizational priorities.
Identify workflow inefficiencies and implement improvements to enhance team effectiveness.
Support CHW professional development through coaching, feedback, and real-time problem-solving.
Perform administrative duties as assigned in the Lead capacity.
Participate in management training sessions and meetings.
Model Malama I Ke Ola’s core values.
Community Outreach & Education
Schedule and coordinate group health education classes.
Develop and distribute education and communication materials in multiple languages using multimodality approaches.
Coordinate and implement community outreach events, including staff engagement communication.
Market community events and CCM programs: create flyers or work with approved vendors; manage event enrollment capacity.
Participate in relevant meetings for program integration with clinical departments and staff.
Systems, Data & Reporting
Identify recurring gaps in patient flow, care coordination, and system processes; recommend and implement workflow improvements.
Support development of standardized processes for SDOH screening, care navigation, and follow-up.
Contribute to data tracking and reporting related to care navigation, patient flow metrics, and/or grant activities.
Compliance & Professional Practice
Practice within the organization’s Clinical Protocols, Guidelines, and Policies and Procedures.
Participate in the clinic’s Emergency Preparedness Plan.

This position is part of the AWS Specialist and Partner (ASP) Organization, within the WW Public Sector partner programs team. AWS Public Sector Competencies recognize AWS Partners who deliver validated, mission-critical solutions for governments, educational institutions, and nonprofits—including the AWS Government Competency, AWS Education Competency, and AWS Nonprofit Competency. These designations help customers instantly identify vetted vendors with specialized expertise in security, compliance, and large-scale public sector procurement.

This role will support the planning and execution of PS Competencies strategy and operations, helping define the strategic direction for how these competencies deliver value to public sector partners. The ideal candidate will evaluate the current program construct, including existing benefits and processes, and shape the go-forward strategy for program applications, partner requirements, and benefit delivery. They will also own operational excellence for the program, refining processes to increase efficiency and leveraging AI tools to automate workflows and scale impact.

In addition to PS Competencies program ownership, this role carries marketing responsibilities for the broader PS Scale Capability Programs portfolio. The successful candidate will plan and execute on-site events, develop program collateral, author blog posts and case studies, and drive measurable business outcomes through integrated marketing motions across PS Scale Capability Programs—not limited to competencies alone. They will work cross-functionally with marketing, program, sales, and in-geo teams to coordinate across stakeholders and deliver results. This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in one of AWS's most impactful partner recognition programs while building a marketing engine that drives awareness, engagement, and partner growth across the PS Scale Capability Programs portfolio.

Program Management & Operations (PS Competencies)

Support the strategic direction for AWS Public Sector Competencies (Government, Education, and Nonprofit), helping define the roadmap and tracking success metrics
Support evaluation of the current application process and benefit construct; contribute to recommendations for the go-forward strategy
Manage partner requirements, application criteria, and benefit frameworks that drive meaningful differentiation for public sector partners
Serve as a key point of contact for PS Competency-related initiatives across internal and external stakeholders
Own day-to-day program operations, ensuring efficient execution of partner applications, reviews, and lifecycle management
Identify operational gaps and implement scalable processes to improve program effectiveness
Leverage AI tools and automation to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort
Track program health, partner engagement, and operational metrics for leadership reporting

Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems, from sensors to spacecraft, that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space—for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra's ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission-ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed.

About The Team

Mission Solutions - The Platforms

Mission Solutions builds on Umbra's expertise in remote sensing and spacecraft operations to engineer platforms purpose-built for U.S. and allied defense and intelligence missions. Whether it's a custom payload, a full-stack spacecraft, or the infrastructure behind an entire constellation, our team delivers secure, resilient systems tailored to exacting requirements and built on timelines that match the urgency of the mission.

If you want to work on cutting-edge space technology that's redefining what's possible in space platforms, you belong here at Umbra.

About The Job

As a Program Manager
at Umbra, you will lead the successful execution of complex government programs, delivering innovative products and mission solutions that meet our customers' objectives while fulfilling contractual commitments. You will be responsible for managing program cost, schedule, technical performance, and customer satisfaction from program kickoff through delivery.

In this role, you will develop and maintain integrated program plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and risk management strategies while partnering closely with engineering, product management, finance, contracts, and operations to ensure successful execution. You'll collaborate with technical teams using Agile development practices, proactively identify and resolve program risks, and provide clear, concise updates to customers and executive leadership.

Success in this role requires strong leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to build trusted relationships with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. By developing a deep understanding of Umbra's technologies and customer missions, you'll help drive program success while supporting follow-on opportunities and the continued growth of our customer partnerships.

This position is based on-site in either our Arlington, VA office or Reston, VA office.

Key Responsibilities

Program Execution: Take complete responsibility for the successful implementation (including cost, schedule, and technical aspects) of several ongoing contracts. Ensure monthly updates of financial results and forecasts. Deliver monthly status reports to facilitate Program Management Reviews.
Processes: Participate in the maturation of Umbra's Program Excellence Framework, which consists of documented procedures for initiating, executing, and concluding programs. Utilize insights and experiences gained from previous programs, while customizing them to align with Umbra's operational style, to establish streamlined processes for areas including financial management, risk management, contractual obligations, and performance monitoring.
Agile Development: Serve as the Business Owner for technologies associated with contracts. Collaborate with product management and system architects on engineering solutions. Engage actively in key Agile ceremonies, including PI planning.

All other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related STEM or business field.
5-8+ years of program management experience, including 2+ years supporting U.S. Government contracts or aerospace and defense programs.
Active TS/SCI security clearance with a read-in within the past two years.
Proven ability to lead complex technical programs and cross-functional teams through planning, execution, and delivery.
Experience supporting U.S. Government captures, proposals, and business development efforts.
Working knowledge of Agile development methodologies and the technology development lifecycle.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across customers, leadership, and cross-functional teams.

Desired Qualifications

10+ years of program management experience, including 4+ years supporting U.S. Government contracts or aerospace and defense programs.
Experience leading complex space or defense programs with responsibility for cost, schedule, technical execution, and customer delivery.
Direct experience supporting space systems, satellite development, mission operations, or remote sensing programs.
Experience with large competitive captures and strategic proposal development.
Experience supporting a broad range of U.S. Government customers, including DoD, Intelligence Community, and Civil agencies.
Familiarity with SAR, RF payloads, and associated ground systems.
Understanding of systems engineering principles, system architectures, and technical development processes.
Familiarity with SAFe, PMI, or other structured program management frameworks.

Role Overview We are seeking a resourceful Volunteer Research Assistant to support three connected areas of our work: research underpinning our AI/ML mental health models, research and identification of grant and funding opportunities, and research supporting the design and evaluation of our community programs. This is a great fit for someone who enjoys digging into primary sources, synthesizing findings into clear briefs, and connecting research to real-world decisions for a mission-driven organization.

•        Support evaluation of open-source Small Language Models (SLMs) and fine-tuning approaches (e.g., LLaMA-based models, QLoRA/PEFT methods) for relevance to BMHM's mental health use cases.
•        Summarize findings on model safety, bias, and appropriateness for use with culturally specific and vulnerable populations.
•        Assist the AI/ML Engineering team by researching evaluation frameworks that help prevent hallucination or harmful outputs in mental health-focused models.
•        Track emerging tools, datasets, and academic research relevant to Black mental health and AI applications.

Grants Research •        Identify and compile grant opportunities (foundation, corporate, and government) aligned with BMHM's mission and current programs.
•        Research eligibility requirements, deadlines, funding priorities, and application processes for prospective funders.
•        Maintain an organized, up-to-date grants pipeline/tracker for the team.
•        Support the drafting of grant research summaries and briefing documents for the Executive Producer and leadership team.
•        Research comparable organizations' funding models and successful grant strategies for reference.

Programs Research •        Research best practices and existing models for community mental health programming, particularly within Black communities.
•        Support the design and evaluation of BMHM programs and initiatives with relevant data, statistics, and comparable case studies.
•        Compile research on mental health outcomes, disparities, and needs specific to the communities BMHM serves.
•        Assist in developing surveys, evaluation frameworks, or feedback tools to help measure program impact.
•        Prepare clear, concise research summaries and briefs for internal program planning discussions.

Mental Health Research Journals & Show Topic Research •        Monitor and review peer-reviewed mental health research journals and academic publications for findings relevant to Black mental health and BMHM's programming.
•        Research and propose timely, culturally relevant topics for upcoming BMHM Show episodes (Panel and One-on-One formats), grounded in current published research.
•        Compile background research briefs on each topic, citing relevant journal articles, statistics, and community context, for hosts and producers.
•        Research potential guests, specialists, and subject-matter experts aligned with proposed topics and published research areas.
•        Maintain an organized reference library/tracker of relevant journal articles and studies for ongoing use by the production and programs teams.
•        Support fact-checking and source verification for claims or statistics used in show scripts and promotional content, citing published research where applicable.

Qualifications & Skills •        Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in a relevant field such as Public Health, Psychology, Social Work, Data Science, Nonprofit Management, or a related discipline.
•        Strong research skills, including the ability to locate, evaluate, and synthesize information from academic, grant, and program-related sources.
•        Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to translate academic research and journal findings into clear, actionable summaries.
•        Basic familiarity with AI/ML concepts and terminology (e.g., LLMs, NLP, model fine-tuning) is a plus; willingness to learn is essential.
•        Prior experience with grant research, grant writing, or nonprofit funding processes is a plus.
•        Familiarity navigating academic/research databases (e.g., PubMed, Google Scholar, PsycINFO) to locate and review peer-reviewed mental health literature.
•        Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage multiple research threads simultaneously.
•        Ability to work independently in a remote, volunteer-based environment.
•        Genuine interest in mental health advocacy and community impact work, particularly within the Black community.

What You'll Gain •        Meaningful, mission-driven volunteer experience across AI/ML research, grants, and program development.
•        Flexible remote schedule (10–20 hrs/week).
•        Collaboration with a passionate, cross-functional team spanning technology, production, and programs.
•        Opportunity to directly influence funding strategy and mental health program design for an underserved community.

new_jobs.description:
Brief Description

PRIMARY FUNCTION

The Lead Community Health Worker (Lead CHW) contributes to meeting patients’ comprehensive needs, including social determinants of health (SDOH) and direct medical services. Under the Primary Care Medical Home (PCMH) model, the Lead CHW contributes to patient recruitment, education, navigation, social support, medical follow-up, care coordination, and integration. Chronic disease management and risk factor reduction are often the focus of these efforts, with emphasis on proven chronic disease prevention and control interventions.

In addition to direct community health work responsibilities, this position serves as the central point of accountability for patient flow across clinical care and community-based services. The Lead CHW translates provider care plans into actionable next steps, oversees daily CHW activities, and resolves breakdowns in referrals, care coordination, and system workflows. This role works across clinical teams, CHWs, and health information systems to close care gaps, prioritize work in real time, and ensure follow-through on care plans.

Join the Malama I Ke Ola Health Center Team!

Team-Based Work Environment
90 Day Introductory Period
Awesome benefits

Medical, Dental, Vision, life insurance, short & long-term disability, and 403(b) Retirement Plan, FSA, and other voluntary benefits

Vacation, Holiday and Sick Benefits

LEAD COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER

with Clinical Navigation Liaison Responsibilities

Essential Duties And Functions

Patient Flow & Care Navigation

The Lead CHW serves as the primary driver of patient movement across clinical and community-based care pathways:

Ensure patients move efficiently from identification of need to completed services across clinical and community-based systems.
Translate provider care plans into clear, actionable tasks for CHWs and care teams.
Monitor and address breakdowns in care pathways, including delays, missed follow-ups, and incomplete referrals.
Prioritize patient needs and direct CHW activities in real time to address urgent or high-risk situations.
Identify High-Needs Patients in collaboration with the Medical Provider; contact all identified High-Needs Patients prior to their next visit to assess whether previous care plan objectives have been completed.
Coordinate pre-visit planning with RN and Medical Provider; review protocols due for the patient.
Support navigation of SDOH needs, ensuring patients are connected to appropriate internal and external resources.
Care Coordination & Community Health Services

The Lead CHW provides direct patient services at the health center and in the community such as:

Care coordination to implement and monitor care management plans
Working with patients, families, caregivers, and community partners
Resource identification, goal setting, and assistance with self-monitoring
Culturally and age-appropriate education in multiple languages, including instructional materials, health screens, and clarification of care plans in compliance with clinical protocols
Patient recruitment: contacting individuals who have not yet established care and informing them about available services
Assistance with appointment scheduling, including contacting patients with no-show or canceled appointment status and rescheduling.
Psychosocial support
Translation and/or interpretation services as qualified
Transportation coordination
Financial assistance to access complementary and alternative care options
Taking vital signs
Assisting with patient-related paperwork
Check, maintain, and report inventory supplies to the Program Manager
Referral Management & Closed-Loop Coordination
Ensure referrals (internal and external) are completed, tracked, and followed through to resolution.
Define and maintain standards for closed-loop referrals and care coordination.
Work with clinical teams to clarify unclear or incomplete referrals and care plans.
Identify and resolve barriers to patient access.
CHW Supervision & Team Leadership

The Lead CHW directly supervises Community Health Workers.

Oversee daily workflow and task prioritization for CHWs; provide real-time direction on patient engagement strategies and care plan execution.
Prepare and publish work schedules; approve timecards and time-off requests in compliance with pay policies.
Recruit, select, train, manage, and motivate CHWs; provide performance feedback during 1:1 sessions and at fiscal year-end.
Ensure CHW activities align with active clinical care plans and organizational priorities.
Identify workflow inefficiencies and implement improvements to enhance team effectiveness.
Support CHW professional development through coaching, feedback, and real-time problem-solving.
Perform administrative duties as assigned in the Lead capacity.
Participate in management training sessions and meetings.
Model Malama I Ke Ola’s core values.
Community Outreach & Education
Schedule and coordinate group health education classes.
Develop and distribute education and communication materials in multiple languages using multimodality approaches.
Coordinate and implement community outreach events, including staff engagement communication.
Market community events and CCM programs: create flyers or work with approved vendors; manage event enrollment capacity.
Participate in relevant meetings for program integration with clinical departments and staff.
Systems, Data & Reporting
Identify recurring gaps in patient flow, care coordination, and system processes; recommend and implement workflow improvements.
Support development of standardized processes for SDOH screening, care navigation, and follow-up.
Contribute to data tracking and reporting related to care navigation, patient flow metrics, and/or grant activities.
Compliance & Professional Practice
Practice within the organization’s Clinical Protocols, Guidelines, and Policies and Procedures.
Participate in the clinic’s Emergency Preparedness Plan.
Participate in self-education as required to maintain patient care competencies.

Provides excellent customer service in-person, over the phone, and during high-stress situations.

Applicants must be 18 years of age or older to be considered for this position

Schedule:

Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday; 7:45AM-4:45PM

We care deeply about supporting our team members — professionally and personally. Benefits include:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Paid Parental Leave (birth, adoption, foster)
401(k) with discretionary contribution
Team Member Pet Discounts
Emotional wellbeing support — including Calm app access and 24/7 EAP
CE stipends and career development resources
Grant Circle — a relief fund for team members facing personal hardship
Local hospital culture backed by national resources

$19—$25 USD

, including 1700+ veterinarians

new_jobs.description:
Description

This position is part of the AWS Specialist and Partner (ASP) Organization, within the WW Public Sector partner programs team. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Program Manager, PS Scale Capability Programs & Partner Engagement to manage day-to-day operations across two interconnected workstreams: (1) the strategy and operations of AWS Public Sector (PS) Competencies, and (2) marketing and events strategy for PS Scale Capability Programs.

AWS Public Sector Competencies recognize AWS Partners who deliver validated, mission-critical solutions for governments, educational institutions, and nonprofits—including the AWS Government Competency, AWS Education Competency, and AWS Nonprofit Competency. These designations help customers instantly identify vetted vendors with specialized expertise in security, compliance, and large-scale public sector procurement.

This role will support the planning and execution of PS Competencies strategy and operations, helping define the strategic direction for how these competencies deliver value to public sector partners. The ideal candidate will evaluate the current program construct, including existing benefits and processes, and shape the go-forward strategy for program applications, partner requirements, and benefit delivery. They will also own operational excellence for the program, refining processes to increase efficiency and leveraging AI tools to automate workflows and scale impact.

In addition to PS Competencies program ownership, this role carries marketing responsibilities for the broader PS Scale Capability Programs portfolio. The successful candidate will plan and execute on-site events, develop program collateral, author blog posts and case studies, and drive measurable business outcomes through integrated marketing motions across PS Scale Capability Programs—not limited to competencies alone. They will work cross-functionally with marketing, program, sales, and in-geo teams to coordinate across stakeholders and deliver results. This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in one of AWS's most impactful partner recognition programs while building a marketing engine that drives awareness, engagement, and partner growth across the PS Scale Capability Programs portfolio.

Key job responsibilities

Program Management & Operations (PS Competencies)

Support the strategic direction for AWS Public Sector Competencies (Government, Education, and Nonprofit), helping define the roadmap and tracking success metrics
Support evaluation of the current application process and benefit construct; contribute to recommendations for the go-forward strategy
Manage partner requirements, application criteria, and benefit frameworks that drive meaningful differentiation for public sector partners
Serve as a key point of contact for PS Competency-related initiatives across internal and external stakeholders
Own day-to-day program operations, ensuring efficient execution of partner applications, reviews, and lifecycle management
Identify operational gaps and implement scalable processes to improve program effectiveness
Leverage AI tools and automation to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort
Track program health, partner engagement, and operational metrics for leadership reporting

Marketing & Events (PS Scale Capability Programs)

Plan and execute on-site events including logistics, speaker coordination, and attendee experience
Develop program collateral and partner-facing materials that communicate the value of PS Scale Capability Programs
Author blog posts, case studies, and thought leadership content showcasing partner success stories
Create presentations, pitch decks, and visual content for diverse audiences
Define event goals and KPIs; measure and report on marketing effectiveness to optimize future initiatives

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work cross-functionally with marketing, program, sales, and in-geo teams to align priorities and execute initiatives
Partner with the WWPS Partner Core enablement lead to co-deliver enablement motions
Support adjacent partner events (TBSB Communities, BOX Partner Matchmaking) ensuring PS Competencies are integrated into broader engagement motions
Coordinate with stakeholders to drive adoption and awareness for PS Competency and PS Scale Capability Programs initiatives
Contribute to business reviews with updates on program operations and marketing outcomes

A day in the life

In this role, you'll split your time between two distinct but complementary workstreams. On the program management side, you'll manage partner applications moving through the competency pipeline, troubleshoot process gaps, coordinate with reviewers, and maintain the operational rhythm of the program. On the marketing side, you'll be building event run-of-shows, drafting partner success stories, creating collateral for upcoming summits, and pulling post-event metrics to inform what's next. You'll regularly coordinate with in-geo teams, the WWPS Partner Core enablement lead, and cross-functional marketing partners. No two weeks look the same — one week you're heads-down on a blog series, the next you're on-site running a partner event.

About The Team

WW Public Sector Partner Core enables partners to accelerate cloud adoption and mission outcomes for public sector customers through scalable partner programs. We work backwards from partner and customer feedback to identify and prioritize the programmatic efforts that will accelerate our partners' success in engaging public sector customers and growing their business on AWS.

The team is globally distributed and works with partners ranging from defense technology startups to global system integrators, supporting Sales teams that cover government, defense, healthcare, education, nonprofit, and aerospace customers worldwide.

This role sits within the Scale Capability pillar of Partner Core and will work closely with cross-functional teams across marketing, partner enablement, and the PS Sales field. It offers broad exposure to how AWS recognizes and grows its public sector partner ecosystem.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of program or project management experience
Experience working on cross-functional projects with multiple stakeholders
Experience creating written content (e.g., blog posts, case studies, presentations, or partner-facing collateral)
Experience using data to track program or campaign performance and inform decisions
Experience planning or supporting events (virtual or in-person)
Proficiency with productivity and project management tools (e.g., Google Workspace, Smartsheet, Asana, or similar)

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a SaaS/technology company or partner-facing environment
Familiarity with partner programs, channel sales, or certification/designation frameworks
Experience with digital marketing, event coordination, or content production
Familiarity with AI tools for process automation and workflow improvement
Experience working in or with public sector organizations (government, education, nonprofit)
Ability to create compelling visual content including presentations and decks
Experience with CRM or partner management platforms
Experience working in ambiguous environments and building programs from the ground up

Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems, from sensors to spacecraft, that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space—for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra's ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission-ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed.

About The Team

Mission Solutions - The Platforms

Mission Solutions builds on Umbra's expertise in remote sensing and spacecraft operations to engineer platforms purpose-built for U.S. and allied defense and intelligence missions. Whether it's a custom payload, a full-stack spacecraft, or the infrastructure behind an entire constellation, our team delivers secure, resilient systems tailored to exacting requirements and built on timelines that match the urgency of the mission.

If you want to work on cutting-edge space technology that's redefining what's possible in space platforms, you belong here at Umbra.

About The Job

As a Program Manager
at Umbra, you will lead the successful execution of complex government programs, delivering innovative products and mission solutions that meet our customers' objectives while fulfilling contractual commitments. You will be responsible for managing program cost, schedule, technical performance, and customer satisfaction from program kickoff through delivery.

In this role, you will develop and maintain integrated program plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and risk management strategies while partnering closely with engineering, product management, finance, contracts, and operations to ensure successful execution. You'll collaborate with technical teams using Agile development practices, proactively identify and resolve program risks, and provide clear, concise updates to customers and executive leadership.

Success in this role requires strong leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to build trusted relationships with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. By developing a deep understanding of Umbra's technologies and customer missions, you'll help drive program success while supporting follow-on opportunities and the continued growth of our customer partnerships.

This position is based on-site in either our Arlington, VA office or Reston, VA office.

Key Responsibilities

Program Execution: Take complete responsibility for the successful implementation (including cost, schedule, and technical aspects) of several ongoing contracts. Ensure monthly updates of financial results and forecasts. Deliver monthly status reports to facilitate Program Management Reviews.
Processes: Participate in the maturation of Umbra's Program Excellence Framework, which consists of documented procedures for initiating, executing, and concluding programs. Utilize insights and experiences gained from previous programs, while customizing them to align with Umbra's operational style, to establish streamlined processes for areas including financial management, risk management, contractual obligations, and performance monitoring.
Agile Development: Serve as the Business Owner for technologies associated with contracts. Collaborate with product management and system architects on engineering solutions. Engage actively in key Agile ceremonies, including PI planning.
Growth and Strategy: Take the lead or provide assistance in developing proposals as needed. Create and implement growth strategies for existing and upcoming contracts. Act as the customer's advocate in product management to help shape company roadmaps based on their requirements.
All other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related STEM or business field.
5-8+ years of program management experience, including 2+ years supporting U.S. Government contracts or aerospace and defense programs.
Active TS/SCI security clearance with a read-in within the past two years.
Proven ability to lead complex technical programs and cross-functional teams through planning, execution, and delivery.
Experience supporting U.S. Government captures, proposals, and business development efforts.
Working knowledge of Agile development methodologies and the technology development lifecycle.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across customers, leadership, and cross-functional teams.

Desired Qualifications

10+ years of program management experience, including 4+ years supporting U.S. Government contracts or aerospace and defense programs.
Experience leading complex space or defense programs with responsibility for cost, schedule, technical execution, and customer delivery.
Direct experience supporting space systems, satellite development, mission operations, or remote sensing programs.
Experience with large competitive captures and strategic proposal development.
Experience supporting a broad range of U.S. Government customers, including DoD, Intelligence Community, and Civil agencies.
Familiarity with SAR, RF payloads, and associated ground systems.
Understanding of systems engineering principles, system architectures, and technical development processes.
Familiarity with SAFe, PMI, or other structured program management frameworks.
Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment with a high degree of ownership and initiative.
Ability to travel domestically (CONUS) up to 25% of the time.

Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, LTD, STD (employer funded)
